slides.title: Design for someone else
slides.text: Today you are the designer. Real teams plan, build, test with someone else, improve the work and document it.
slides.alt: The Pro Level Maker opens its first task: a blank canvas and the tools to build a level for someone else.

slides.title: Keep a timeline
slides.text: Split the work and set times: build by minute 6, test by 12, fix by 18. Write who does each part.
slides.alt: A second Pro maker task: the brief sets what to build, the way a team plan sets who does each part and by when.

slides.title: Feedback is information
slides.text: Feedback is not a grade. It shows where a player got stuck. A level is done when that feedback changed something and you tested it again.
slides.alt: After the test play, the maker rates the level: the feedback card records how fun and how hard the tester found it.

slides.title: Iterate
slides.text: Going round this loop is called iteration. Check proves the level can be solved and shows its par.
slides.alt: A Pro maker level built and checked: the board holds a full design and Check has judged whether it can be solved.

slides.title: Write the level note
slides.text: A good note helps the next person play or remix it, like: Level 2: count the gems before the door. The game saves your level and its code, so write the note on paper with the code at the top. Remixed levels keep their based-on stamp.
slides.alt: A second Pro maker task: the brief sets what to build, the way a team plan sets who does each part and by when.

words.means: one more round of build, test and improve
what testers tell you about where they got stuck
notes that explain your work to the next person

slides.title: Dot is waiting
slides.text: Every piece you light makes the Spark warmer. The next world belongs to Dot the fox, who follows clues the way you follow code. She is already sniffing at the door.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Robo Route at Level Maker and do the three maker tasks to finish this step. Then, as a stretch, build your own level from a plan, let someone test it in silence, and change one thing. Write its level note on paper, with the level code at the top.
slides.alt: The Pro Level Maker opens its first task: a blank canvas and the tools to build a level for someone else.
